title: Let code AST nodes link to external technical corpora without absorbing their models
description: Building Code AST can preserve a citation and target domain; a related ontology or graph can resolve that target to listing, product, or certification evidence.
author: bcast

title: The ownership boundary is active while the cross-corpus link model remains open
description: The code tree stays focused on source structure. Exact interchange identities and ontology semantics remain future evidence-backed design work.
author: bcast

title: Make every derived structure auditable without confusing it with authoritative source text
description: Parser output must identify what source, edition, region, parser, and transformation produced it and what remains uncertain or unreviewed.
author: bcast

title: Record source artifact, edition, page or region, printed locator, and exact extraction span
description: Structural claims remain traceable to the evidence from which they were derived, including source coordinates when the adapter can supply them.
author: bcast

title: Record parser version, transformation history, diagnostics, and review state where contracts support them
description: Confidence is a review aid, not a legal probability; deterministic lexical methods and explicit review status are preferable to unlabeled inference.
author: bcast

title: Separate evidence role, access scope, and rights status
description: A source may be available to the owner without permission to redistribute it. Registration guards exact bytes and records restricted or uncertain publication boundaries.
author: bcast

title: Label ASTs, expected changelogs, and projections as derived evidence
description: Generated structure can be deterministic and reviewed while the issued publication remains controlling. Development history, errata, and amendments retain their own evidence roles.
author: bcast

title: The repository publishes contracts and synthetic evidence while text-bearing outputs stay private
description: Public Git contains project-authored software, schemas, documentation, diagnostics, aggregate receipts, and synthetic fixtures rather than copyrighted source corpora.
author: bcast

title: Preserve malformed, ambiguous, or unsupported content instead of dropping it
description: Unsupported regions, unresolved references, blocked action chains, and diagnostics keep absence from masquerading as successful parsing.
author: bcast

title: Validate parser claims against source evidence and invariants
description: A parser is trustworthy only when its output is deterministic, source-located, structurally legal, and bounded to the regions actually reviewed.
author: bcast

title: Compare extracted fragments against source locations and known-good references
description: Production audits check retained and excluded fragments, source spans, reading order, hierarchy records, and representative golden cases without publishing source prose.
author: bcast

title: Enforce identity, span, containment, uniqueness, ordering, and parent-child invariants
description: Document and family-specific validators reject duplicate locators, out-of-parent spans, malformed ancestry, unresolved required parents, and nondeterministic identities.
author: bcast

title: Validate table partitions, figure support claims, and cross-reference resolution separately
description: A table boundary, a semantic table interpretation, a figure reference, and a resolved target are different claims and receive different checks or diagnostics.
author: bcast

title: Use public synthetic fixtures and private source replay together
description: Synthetic fixtures make contracts reproducible; private exact-source runs expose real layout defects; neither alone proves complete-edition support.
author: bcast

title: Official corpus replay exposed adapter defects after initial implementation
description: ICC proposal/action separation, Washington leaf-span layout, sequence preservation, and unsupported-action boundaries required multiple post-merge corrections.
author: bcast

title: Reconcile PR claims against merge state, current tree, tests, and generated outputs
description: Open or superseded branch results are recorded as branch evidence; current support is never inferred from a PR description alone.
author: bcast

title: Keep source structure reusable without absorbing jurisdiction, product lineage, or compliance logic
description: The AST should expose stable evidence-bearing structures that downstream systems can combine with their own authority and domain models.
author: bcast

title: Building Code Map owns location, authority, adoption, amendment applicability, and permit-context resolution
description: A code clause cannot determine which jurisdiction or edition applies to an address; that requires geocoding, boundary resolution, policy evidence, and time-aware adoption data.
author: bcast

title: Electrical Equipment Lineage owns manufacturer, product, UL, and replacement evidence
description: Code references can connect to that corpus, but certification history and equipment compatibility remain separate evidence domains.
author: bcast

title: Model jurisdictional amendments as source-backed patches against an identified base publication state
description: The repository can represent add, replace, delete, reserve, and scope evidence without deciding the governing jurisdiction or rendering a legally controlling consolidated code.
author: bcast

title: Keep compliance and engineering reasoning out of the source-structure repository
description: Future tools may resolve definitions, conditions, exceptions, amendments, products, and project facts, but they must consume provenance rather than mutate the canonical source tree.
author: bcast

title: Building Code AST remains a bounded compiler and evidence substrate
description: Downstream products can compare clauses, reconcile expected changes, resolve amendments, and link technical corpora while this repository preserves source structure and parser truthfulness.
author: bcast

title: Make architecture decisions, parser limits, and verification evidence maintainable
description: As the repository accumulated source families and branch experiments, its documentation needed accepted history, generated views, and exact-head verification without duplicating another knowledge system.
author: bcast

title: Recreate LORE-style records and renderers inside the repository
description: The first interpretation duplicated LORE rather than using its shipped skill and transaction model, creating a parallel maintenance mechanism.
author: bcast

title: Adopt LORE itself and its shipped maintenance skill
description: The repository pins the trust root, records accepted semantic history and a transaction receipt, and generates non-authoritative projections through LORE.
author: bcast

title: Add Deciduous as a non-authoritative causal archaeology layer
description: The graph explains why models and parser boundaries changed. Repository code, schemas, tests, accepted LORE records, and source publications remain authoritative for current behavior.
author: bcast

title: Current main supports shared AST contracts, selected NEC 2017 workflows, and publication evidence adapters
description: Main contains Document AST, Provision AST 0.2.0, NEC Articles 90/100/110 ingestion and hierarchy/semantics, source register, ICC errata/development adapters, and Washington amendment adapters.
author: bcast

title: IBC 2018, NFPA 13 2019, NEC 2020 expected changes, and Provision AST 0.3 remain branch-bound
description: These branches contain substantial work or design evidence, but none may be labeled current main support or complete-edition coverage.
author: bcast

title: The durable contract is provenance-first, family-specific, fail-closed, and explicitly bounded
description: New datasets expand evidence only after source-safe ingestion, family grammar, deterministic projections, source review, and support-claim qualification. Open research remains marked unresolved.
author: bcast

title: Engineers navigate and cite code by sections and subsections, not PDF pages
description: PDF pagination varies across editions, printings, and source files, while the publication's own section hierarchy is the durable coordinate engineers use.
author: bcast

title: Make published code addresses the primary identity and navigation surface
description: Sections, subsections, tables, figures, exceptions, definitions, and equations become canonical navigation coordinates. Page numbers cannot supply fallback structural identities.
author: bcast

title: Retain PDF coordinates only as secondary provenance
description: PDF pages, printed-page labels, offsets, bounding boxes, and raw block locators remain available for source reproduction and parser debugging, while navigation, relationships, ordering, and edition comparison use structural code addresses.
author: bcast
